transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, I guess what finally made me come in is I keep forgetting these little things I’m usually the one who handles. Like I’ll mean to return a call, or I’ll have a registration form that needs turning in, or I’m supposed to stop somewhere on the way home, and then it just… doesn’t happen. And I know everybody forgets things, but it’s been enough lately that I’m getting frustrated with myself.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Um… I don’t think so? Not really “depressed,” at least not in the way I think of it. I get frustrated with myself, like when I mess something up that should’ve been simple, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down all the time.

Sorry, I know that’s not a very clean answer. I guess I’m just not sure where the line is between being stressed and being depressed.
Have you had trouble with attention or forgetfulness like this since you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, looking back, even in elementary school I was kind of that kid who’d forget the permission slip was due, or my homework would be done but somehow lost in my backpack. My mom used to have to check with me step by step, like, “Did you put it in the folder? Did you put the folder in your bag?” 

And teachers too, with projects — I’d need reminders for each part. I don’t know, at the time it just felt like I was messy or not trying hard enough. But yes, it was there when I was little.
Do these attention and forgetfulness problems cause trouble for you in more than one part of your life, like both at work and at home?

Yeah, I think it does show up in more than one place. At work, I’m mostly keeping things together, but I’ve missed little follow-ups — like not getting back to someone or forgetting to pass something along — and those are the kind of things people notice in an office.

And at home it’s more school-related stuff, like deadlines for forms or things my family is counting on me to remember. I mean, I’m still functioning, it’s not like everything is falling apart, but it’s happened enough that I worry people will think I’m unreliable. Especially at work, because I’ve been hoping maybe I could move toward an Office Manager role, and then I think, well, who’s going to trust me with more if I’m missing small things now?
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks or conversations, even when you’re trying to pay attention?

Yes… yeah, I do. Even when I’m really trying to listen or finish something, it doesn’t take much to knock me off track.

Like at the office, if a phone rings or two people start talking nearby, I’ll look up and then suddenly I’ve lost where I was. Or I’ll be in the middle of something and have this random thought like, “Oh, did I remember to take care of that thing at home?” and then my brain kind of follows that instead.

It’s annoying because I’m not trying to ignore people or be careless. I’ll be making an effort, and then I realize I’ve drifted.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to deal with?

Um… I’m not sure I’d call it a lot. I mean, I worry about normal stuff, I guess — like whether I remembered something or if something is coming up — but I don’t know if it’s more than other people.

Sometimes I’ll get caught thinking about things, but then again, everyone in my family kind of does that. My mom used to make lists for everything, like grocery lists with little boxes next to them, and I always thought that was just how adults keep track of life.

So… I guess I’d say I haven’t really noticed myself worrying for no reason all the time. It’s more when there’s something I think I might be missing.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Yeah, kind of. I wouldn’t say I’m, like, pacing around all the time or anything, but if I have to sit for a long time, I notice it.

Like during longer classes or trainings, I’ll be clicking my pen, or bouncing my foot, or shifting around in the chair even though I’m trying to just sit still and pay attention. I used to think maybe everyone did that, because those chairs are never comfortable anyway, and then I’ll start thinking about how schools all have the same terrible chairs— sorry, that’s not really the point.

But yes, I do fidget when I’m sitting for a while.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks, like figuring out the steps and keeping materials in order?

Yeah… especially lately. I can usually keep up at work because I’ve got routines there, like certain forms go in certain places and I kind of know the order things happen in.

But since I started evening classes, it’s gotten messier. My desk ends up with stacks of papers, my class folder gets stuffed with everything instead of sorted, and I’ll set email reminders but then they all pile up too. Then I waste time just trying to figure out, okay, what am I actually supposed to do first?

And then I’ll find, like, an old handout or a note I wrote to myself and get sidetracked trying to remember why I wrote it… So yes, organizing tasks is definitely harder than I’d like.
Did these symptoms get noticeably worse after you started your evening classes?

Yeah, I think so. It’s not like they suddenly appeared out of nowhere, but they’ve been noticeably harder to manage since I started the evening certificate program.

That was… about 15 months ago now, I think? I remember because I bought this big planner at the start of it, like I was going to become a totally organized person overnight, and then I kept forgetting to actually use the planner. But yes — since starting those evening classes, the attention and organization stuff has felt harder to keep on top of.
Since starting the evening classes, have you been feeling more stressed than usual?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I guess evening classes are stressful in the way anything extra after work is stressful, but I don’t know if I’d say I’ve been more stressed than usual in some clear way.

Sometimes I’ll feel kind of overloaded just trying to get there and keep track of things, and then I start thinking about dinner or laundry or whether I forgot to answer someone’s email—sorry, that’s not really answering. I guess I haven’t really noticed stress as the main thing, if that makes sense.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had moments where I’m frustrated or kind of tired, especially when I’m behind on things, but “down or depressed most of the day nearly every day” sounds… stronger than what I’ve noticed.

I guess I haven’t really been tracking my mood day by day, though. Like if you asked me what I felt last Tuesday, I’d probably have to look at my calendar and even then—sorry, I’m going off. But no, I don’t think I’ve been depressed like that over the past couple weeks.
Do you often interrupt people or blurt things out before they’ve finished speaking?

Um… I don’t think that’s a big thing for me? I mean, I probably do it sometimes, like if I’m excited or I think of something before I forget it, but I don’t know if people would say I’m constantly interrupting.

At work I try pretty hard not to, because, you know, phones and scheduling and everyone already talking over each other sometimes—actually our front desk gets chaotic in a way that makes it hard to tell who interrupted who. But blurting things out before someone’s done… I haven’t really noticed that as a regular problem.
When you have a lighter week with fewer classes or responsibilities, do your attention and forgetfulness problems get noticeably better?

A little, maybe, but not enough that it just goes away. Like if I have fewer classes, there’s less to juggle, so obviously I’m not forgetting class-related stuff as much. But the thing that made me finally ask for help was that I started forgetting these little everyday things I usually handle fine—returning calls, turning in a registration form, stopping for an errand on the way home.

And then I’ll remember later, usually at some inconvenient time, like when I’m already home and have my shoes off. So a lighter week helps some, I guess, but the forgetfulness is still there.
Over the past six months, have you felt worried or on edge more days than not?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I worry about things sometimes, like anyone does, especially if there’s something coming up or I’ve got a lot on my plate, but “more days than not” over six months… I don’t know.

Six months is kind of hard for me to look back on all at once. I can remember specific weeks better if something big was happening, but in general I haven’t really been keeping track of whether I felt on edge day to day. So… I wouldn’t want to say yes for sure.
Do you often act on impulse, like doing or saying things before thinking them through?

I’m not sure I’d call myself impulsive exactly. I mean, I’ll sometimes say something and then think afterward, “Oh, I probably could’ve worded that better,” but I don’t know if that’s the same thing.

Doing things before thinking them through… not that I’ve noticed as a big pattern. I tend to overthink more than jump into things, honestly. Although at work, if the phone is ringing and someone’s standing there waiting, I might just answer quickly and then realize I didn’t finish something else—but that’s more like being busy, I think. So… I don’t really know. It doesn’t feel like one of my main problems.
Do you often put off starting tasks that require a lot of mental effort?

Yeah… I think so. Especially if it’s something where I have to really sit down and use my brain for a while, like reading a long chapter or writing out a plan for something. I’ll tell myself I’m going to do it after dinner, and then I’ll end up doing dishes or checking one quick thing, or suddenly I remember the laundry—though sometimes I think I use those things as an excuse.

Then it gets late, and I’m tired after work, and I’m rushing through it, which is not ideal. It’s not that I never do it, I just… getting started is the part I keep putting off.
Do you often find yourself unable to stop or control your worrying?

I’m not really sure. I do worry sometimes, but “unable to stop” sounds a little stronger than what I’d usually say. Like, if something is coming up, I might keep thinking about it while I’m doing other things, but then sometimes I get distracted by something else anyway.

It’s hard for me to separate normal worrying from, like, a bigger problem. I don’t think I’ve noticed it as something I can never control… but I also don’t always pay close attention to it.
Since starting the evening classes, have you often felt overwhelmed?

Yeah, I have felt kind of overwhelmed since starting the evening classes. I can usually keep things together at work—like, I’m not perfect, but I manage. But now with class added in, it’s like everything turns into a pile.

My desk will have work papers, then my class folder gets stuffed with handouts, and then I’ll have email reminders sitting there and I don’t know which one I’m supposed to deal with first. I spend way too much time just sorting through things instead of actually doing them. Like yesterday I was trying to find one class thing, and then I found an old form from work that I forgot to file, and then I started doing that instead… so yes, I guess overwhelmed is the right word.
Do you feel your current problems are mainly a reaction to the stress of starting the evening classes?

I mean, the classes definitely made it more obvious, but I don’t think it’s only from that. Like, this kind of thing goes way back for me.

Even in elementary school, I was always the kid who forgot permission slips or had homework somewhere in my backpack but couldn’t find it. My mom or my teacher would have to remind me step by step to finish projects, otherwise I’d sort of lose track of what I was supposed to be doing. I remember those big poster board projects—sorry, this is probably not what you asked exactly—but I’d have the markers and pictures all over the table and then just not know what order to do it in.

So… the evening classes are stressing me out, yes, but it feels like they’re bringing out problems I already had, not creating them from nowhere.
Do you often make careless mistakes or miss details when you’re doing work or school tasks?

Um… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean, I probably do sometimes, like anyone does, but I don’t know if it’s “often.” At work I try to double-check things because if I don’t, I get nervous I might miss something, especially with forms or emails.

School tasks are a little harder to say. I’ll think I read the instructions, and then later realize there was some small part I didn’t pay attention to—but I don’t know if that counts as careless mistakes or just me being tired after work. Sorry, I’m kind of thinking of this one time with a class handout, but that’s probably not the best example. So… I guess I’ve noticed it sometimes, but I’m not sure how frequent it is.

doctor.question: Do you often act on impulse, like doing or saying things before thinking them through?

target_item.reason: The question is about impulsive actions or speech before thinking, which is not covered by the listed symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I’d call myself impulsive exactly. I mean, I’ll sometimes say something and then think afterward, “Oh, I probably could’ve worded that better,” but I don’t know if that’s the same thing.

Doing things before thinking them through… not that I’ve noticed as a big pattern. I tend to overthink more than jump into things, honestly. Although at work, if the phone is ringing and someone’s standing there waiting, I might just answer quickly and then realize I didn’t finish something else—but that’s more like being busy, I think. So… I don’t really know. It doesn’t feel like one of my main problems.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the patient has another core adult ADHD symptom that would strengthen ADHD over stress/anxiety-related explanations.
doctor.question: Do you often put off starting tasks that require a lot of mental effort?

target_item.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
target_item.manifestation: If an assignment means sitting down to read a long chapter or write out a plan, I keep putting it off until it’s late and then I’m rushing through it after work.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about procrastinating or avoiding tasks that require sustained mental effort, which directly matches this symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. Especially if it’s something where I have to really sit down and use my brain for a while, like reading a long chapter or writing out a plan for something. I’ll tell myself I’m going to do it after dinner, and then I’ll end up doing dishes or checking one quick thing, or suddenly I remember the laundry—though sometimes I think I use those things as an excuse.

Then it gets late, and I’m tired after work, and I’m rushing through it, which is not ideal. It’s not that I never do it, I just… getting started is the part I keep putting off.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether there is clinically significant anxiety that could point toward generalized anxiety disorder rather than ADHD alone.
doctor.question: Do you often find yourself unable to stop or control your worrying?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about inability to control worrying, which relates to anxiety rather than any symptom item covered in the provided ADHD symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure. I do worry sometimes, but “unable to stop” sounds a little stronger than what I’d usually say. Like, if something is coming up, I might keep thinking about it while I’m doing other things, but then sometimes I get distracted by something else anyway.

It’s hard for me to separate normal worrying from, like, a bigger problem. I don’t think I’ve noticed it as something I can never control… but I also don’t always pay close attention to it.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the worsening after starting evening classes reflects an adjustment-related emotional response rather than baseline ADHD symptoms.
doctor.question: Since starting the evening classes, have you often felt overwhelmed?

target_item.name: Organization_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: I can usually keep up at work, but since starting the evening classes my desk, class folder, and email reminders all turn into piles, and I waste time figuring out what I’m supposed to do first.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I have felt kind of overwhelmed since starting the evening classes. I can usually keep things together at work—like, I’m not perfect, but I manage. But now with class added in, it’s like everything turns into a pile.

My desk will have work papers, then my class folder gets stuffed with handouts, and then I’ll have email reminders sitting there and I don’t know which one I’m supposed to deal with first. I spend way too much time just sorting through things instead of actually doing them. Like yesterday I was trying to find one class thing, and then I found an old form from work that I forgot to file, and then I started doing that instead… so yes, I guess overwhelmed is the right word.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the recent worsening is specifically linked to a stressor and exceeds what would be expected from longstanding ADHD, helping distinguish adjustment disorder from ADHD alone.
doctor.question: Do you feel your current problems are mainly a reaction to the stress of starting the evening classes?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Even in elementary school, I was the kid who forgot permission slips, lost homework in my backpack, and needed my mother or teacher to remind me step by step to finish projects.
target_item.reason: The question is asking whether the current problems are only a reaction to recent class-related stress, and this item addresses that the attention and organization difficulties were present since childhood, before the evening classes.

patient.answer:
I mean, the classes definitely made it more obvious, but I don’t think it’s only from that. Like, this kind of thing goes way back for me.

Even in elementary school, I was always the kid who forgot permission slips or had homework somewhere in my backpack but couldn’t find it. My mom or my teacher would have to remind me step by step to finish projects, otherwise I’d sort of lose track of what I was supposed to be doing. I remember those big poster board projects—sorry, this is probably not what you asked exactly—but I’d have the markers and pictures all over the table and then just not know what order to do it in.

So… the evening classes are stressing me out, yes, but it feels like they’re bringing out problems I already had, not creating them from nowhere.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the attention symptoms reflect the remaining core adult ADHD criterion of making careless mistakes or missing details, to distinguish ADHD from stress/anxiety-related distractibility or memory complaints.
doctor.question: Do you often make careless mistakes or miss details when you’re doing work or school tasks?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about careless mistakes or missing details, but the provided symptom profiles do not include an item specifically covering that symptom.

patient.answer:
Um… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean, I probably do sometimes, like anyone does, but I don’t know if it’s “often.” At work I try to double-check things because if I don’t, I get nervous I might miss something, especially with forms or emails.

School tasks are a little harder to say. I’ll think I read the instructions, and then later realize there was some small part I didn’t pay attention to—but I don’t know if that counts as careless mistakes or just me being tired after work. Sorry, I’m kind of thinking of this one time with a class handout, but that’s probably not the best example. So… I guess I’ve noticed it sometimes, but I’m not sure how frequent it is.

Symptoms predate the recent evening classes and are only exacerbated by increased demands, supporting ADHD rather than a primary stress/anxiety or depressive disorder.
